title: The Birth of Opera
objective: After this level you can explain how opera began in Italy around 1600.
summary: Opera grew from Florence's Camerata, which tried to revive Greek music. Peri's La Dafne (1598) was probably the first opera. Recitative carries the plot; the aria carries the feeling.

cards.headline: Opera was invented by people trying to bring back ancient Greece.
cards.body: In Florence, a circle of poets, musicians and thinkers set out to revive the music of ancient Greece. Nobody knew exactly how it had sounded. What came out of their work was something brand new: opera.

cards.headline: The Camerata's idea: one voice, clearly heard
cards.body: The group, called the Camerata, met in Florence around 1573 to 87 under Count Giovanni Bardi; Vincenzo Galilei, father of the astronomer Galileo, was a member. Their efforts helped produce monody: one expressive solo voice over simple chords, a sharp turn from the many interwoven voices of Renaissance polyphony. Out of that grew Jacopo Peri's La Dafne in 1598, probably the first opera.

cards.headline: Two ways to sing a story
cards.body: Opera sings its story in two modes. Recitative imitates the rhythms and accents of speech, using only a few pitches, and it carries the dialogue and plot. The aria is where emotion pours out in melody. Talk, then feel, then talk again. Handel's oratorios borrowed the same tools: in Messiah, recitatives move the story forward and set up the arias and choruses.

mascot.line: Recitative talks, aria feels. Keep those two jobs apart and opera makes sense.

questions.prompt: What was Florence's Camerata trying to do when its work led toward opera?

options.label: Revive the music of ancient Greece
Write new music for the Pope
options.rationale: Their model was ancient Greece, not the Church.

options.label: Build Europe's first public theater
options.rationale: Venice's public opera house came later, in 1637.

options.label: Invent a new kind of violin
options.rationale: They were after a style of singing, not an instrument.

questions.explanation: The Camerata tried to revive ancient Greek music, and its monody fed the first operas.

questions.prompt: In an early opera, a character rattles through a plot twist in speech-like singing. What is that part called?

options.label: An aria
options.rationale: The aria pauses the action for emotion.

options.label: An overture
options.rationale: An overture is instrumental, before the action.

options.label: A chorus
options.rationale: A chorus is a group; this is speech-like solo singing.

questions.explanation: Recitative follows the rhythm of speech and carries the dialogue and plot.

questions.prompt: Level 34's Messiah is an oratorio, not an opera. What job do its recitatives do?

options.label: They repeat the Hallelujah chorus
options.rationale: The chorus is a separate number.

options.label: They pause the action for big emotions

questions.explanation: Just as in opera, Messiah's recitatives move the story forward and set up arias and choruses.
